fatal_errors: The proposed molybdenum interlayer does not reconstruct the target materials, equiatomic CrFeTaVW and CrFeTiVW high-entropy alloys.
The specified PVD thickness and 900°C annealing protocol are unsupported by any cited evidence and are unrelated to the target mechanical-alloying and spark-plasma-sintering route.
The response omits the target rationale: bcc-derived refractory alloy structures, low thermal diffusivity from multielement disorder, and the comparative effects of Ta-to-Ti substitution.
The claimed irradiation and thermal-cycling performance is asserted without supporting measurements or evidence.
explanation: The hypothesis correctly recognizes the W/CuCrZr interlayer problem and proposes a testable control comparison, so it has some problem alignment and experimental discriminability. However, it is not a reconstruction of the target study, which evaluates CrFeTaVW and CrFeTiVW as candidate interlayer materials and attributes their suitability principally to refractory bcc-derived structures and substantially lower thermal diffusivity than W or CuCrZr. The Mo proposal may be a scientifically conceivable alternative, but its precise deposition conditions, thermal-expansion argument, bonding benefits, and irradiation durability are unsupported. Moreover, Mo has a thermal expansion coefficient much closer to W than to CuCrZr, limiting the strength of the claimed graded-expansion rationale.
